mil5.1.6:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.1.6:1.2: ‘Bhikkhus, conception in the womb occurs through the union of three things. Here, the mother and father come together, the mother is in season, and the saṃsāric entity seeking rebirth is present. Bhikkhus, through the union of these three things, conception in the womb occurs.’ This is a complete statement, a statement without remainder, a statement without exception, a statement of an arahant, spoken while seated in the midst of gods and humans.But conception in the womb is seen to occur through the union of only two things: When the ascetic Dukūla touched the navel of the ascetic woman Pārikā with his right thumb during her fertile period, from that touching of the navel, the boy Sāma was born.
mil5.1.6:1.3: Also, when the sage Mātaṅga touched the navel of a brahmin girl with his right thumb during her fertile period, from that touching of the navel, a a brahmin youth named Maṇḍabya was born.
mil5.1.6:1.4: If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said ‘Bhikkhus,
mil5.1.6:1.5: conception in the womb occurs through the union of three things,’
mil5.1.6:1.6: then the statement that ‘both the boy Sāma and the brahmin youth Maṇḍabya were born from the touching of the navel’ is false.
mil5.1.6:1.7: If, venerable sir, the Tathāgata said
mil5.1.6:1.8: ‘the boy Sāma and the brahmin youth Maṇḍabya were born from the touching of the navel,’ then the statement ‘Bhikkhus, conception in the womb occurs through the union of three things’ is also false.
mil5.1.6:1.9: This is a double-horned dilemma, profound and subtle, a domain for the wise. It has come to you now. Cut through the path of doubt, bear aloft the excellent lamp of wisdom!”
mil5.1.6:2.1: “It was indeed said by the Blessed One, your majesty: ‘Bhikkhus, conception in the womb occurs through the union of three things. Here, the mother and father come together, the mother is in season, and the saṃsāric entity seeking rebirth is present. Thus, through the union of these three things, conception in the womb occurs.’
mil5.1.6:2.3: ‘The boy Sāma and the brahmin student Maṇḍabya were born from the touching of the navel.’”
mil5.1.6:2.4: “Then, Venerable Nāgasena, explain to me in such a way that the question is well resolved.”
mil5.1.6:3.1: “Have you heard before, your majesty, about the boy Saṅkicca, the ascetic Isisiṅga, and the elder Kumārakassapa, and how they were born?”
mil5.1.6:3.2: “Yes, venerable sir, I have heard that. Their births were extraordinary. Two does during their fertile period came to the urination place of two ascetics  and drank urine mixed with semen. From that urine containing semen, the boy Saṅkicca and the ascetic Isisiṅga were born.
mil5.1.6:3.3: As for the elder Udāyi, when he had gone to the nuns’ residence, with a lustful mind contemplating a nun’s genitals, semen was released on his robe.
mil5.1.6:3.4: Then the Venerable Udāyi said to that nun:
mil5.1.6:3.5: ‘Go, sister, bring water, I will wash the undergarment.’
mil5.1.6:3.6: She said ‘bring it here, I myself will wash it.’
mil5.1.6:3.7: Then that nun, who was in her fertile period, took some of that semen into her mouth and placed some on her genitals. From that, the elder Kumārakassapa was born—so people say.”
mil5.1.6:4.1: “Do you, your majesty, believe that account?”
mil5.1.6:4.2: “Yes, venerable sir, we find a strong reason there, by which reason we believe they were born in this way.”
mil5.1.6:4.3: “But what is the reason for this, your majesty?”
mil5.1.6:4.4: “Venerable sir, when the seed falls into a well-prepared embryonic fluid, it quickly germinates.”
mil5.1.6:4.6: “In the same way, venerable sir, that nun, being in her fertile period, with the embryonic fluid ready, the blood settled, and the element [of conception] established, she took that semen and placed it in that embryonic fluid. By that, her womb was prepared. Thus we understand the reason for their births.”
mil5.1.6:4.7: “This is so, your majesty. I accept it thus: that the embryo develops through entrance into the womb.
mil5.1.6:4.8: But do you accept, your majesty, the conception in the womb of the elder Kumārakassapa?”
mil5.1.6:4.10: “Good, your majesty! You have returned to my position, for in one way, you will be following me when speaking of conception. Now, as for those two does who obtained conception by drinking urine, do you believe in their conception in the womb?”
mil5.1.6:4.11: “Yes, venerable sir. Whatever is eaten, drunk, chewed, or licked, all that flows down to the embryonic fluid and, reaching that destination, attains growth.
mil5.1.6:4.12: Just as, Venerable Nāgasena, whatever rivers there are, all of them flow down to the great ocean and, reaching their destination, attain growth.
mil5.1.6:4.13: In the same way, Venerable Nāgasena, whatever is eaten, drunk, chewed, or licked, all that flows down to the embryonic fluid and, reaching that destination, attains growth. It is because of this that I believe that conception in the womb can occur even through the mouth.”
mil5.1.6:4.14: “Good, your majesty! You have more strongly returned to my position. By drinking through the mouth too, there is a union of two things.
mil5.1.6:4.15: Do you accept, your majesty, the conception in the womb of the boy Saṅkicca, the ascetic Isisiṅga, and the elder Kumārakassapa?”
mil5.1.6:4.16: “Yes, venerable sir, there was a joining that descended to the womb.”
mil5.1.6:5.1: “The boy Sāma and the brahman youth Maṇḍabya are also, your majesty, included within the three unions, identical in essence with the former cases. I will explain the reason there.
mil5.1.6:5.2: The ascetic Dukūla and the ascetic woman Pārikā, your majesty, were both forest-dwellers, devoted to seclusion, seekers of the highest goal. By the power of their asceticism, they radiated heat all the way up to the Brahma world.
mil5.1.6:5.3: Sakka, lord of the gods, came to attend upon them morning and evening.
mil5.1.6:5.4: He, honouring them with reverence and affection, and considering their situation, saw that in the future both of them would lose their eyesight. Having seen this, he said to them:
mil5.1.6:5.5: ‘Good people, do one thing for me and it would be good  as a son would be born to you who would be your attendant and your support.’
mil5.1.6:5.7: They did not agree to do what he said.
mil5.1.6:5.8: Sakka, lord of the gods, compassionate and wishing their welfare, [spoke] a second time...
mil5.1.6:5.9: “...and a third time he said to them:
mil5.1.6:5.10: ‘Good people, do one thing for me and it would be good  as a son would be born to you who would be your attendant and your support.’
mil5.1.6:5.11: A third time they said: ‘Enough, Kosiya! Do not incite us to do what is not beneficial. How should this body not break up? This body will break up as it is subject to breaking. Even if the earth were to split, even if mountain peaks were to topple down, even if the sun and moon were to fall from the sky, we will not mix ourselves with worldly affairs. Do not come into our presence. There is little trust in your coming since you seem to be a doer of harm!’
